title: Archaeologists Are Reconstructing the 'Invisible' Technologies of the Stone Age
title_zh: 考古学家正在重建石器时代的“隐形”技术

paragraphs.zh: 订阅《史密森尼》杂志，即可获赠一个免费手提袋。

paragraphs.en: Largely missing from the archaeological record, fiber innovations played a huge role in the lives of early humans. Researchers are weaving together new insights from the traces they left behind
paragraphs.zh: 纤维创新在考古记录中大多缺失，但它们在早期人类的生活中发挥了巨大作用。 研究人员正在将他们留下的痕迹所带来的新见解编织在一起

sents.en: Largely missing from the archaeological record, fiber innovations played a huge role in the lives of early humans.
sents.zh: 纤维创新在考古记录中大多缺失，但它们在早期人类的生活中发挥了巨大作用。

sents.en: Researchers are weaving together new insights from the traces they left behind
sents.zh: 研究人员正在将他们留下的痕迹所带来的新见解编织在一起

paragraphs.en: In the lab, archaeologists showed how they could rapidly produce thick rope by threading cattail fibers through a replica of a Stone Age tool.
paragraphs.zh: 在实验室里，考古学家展示了如何通过将香蒲纤维穿入一件石器时代工具的复制品中，快速制作出粗绳索。

paragraphs.en: When an abstract-looking ivory artifact emerged from the Hohle Fels cave in southern Germany in 2015, archaeologists didn’t know quite what to make of it. Previously, this same cave had yielded what may be the world’s oldest musical flutes, as well as one of humanity’s earliest pieces of figurative art, the iconic Venus of Hohle Fels . At first glance, the strange new discovery—a nearly eight-inch rod perforated with four small holes—seemed comparatively unspectacular. But it has since revealed far more about the lives of Europe’s prehistoric hunter-gatherers than its unassuming appearance might have suggested.
paragraphs.zh: 2015年，当一件外形抽象的象牙制品从德国南部的霍勒费尔斯洞穴出土时，考古学家并不太清楚该如何解读它。 此前，同一座洞穴曾出土过可能是世界上最古老的骨笛，以及人类最早的具象艺术作品之一——标志性的霍勒费尔斯维纳斯雕像。 乍一看，这一奇特的新发现——一根近八英寸长、穿有四个小孔的杆状物——似乎相对而言并不起眼。 但此后它所揭示的关于欧洲史前狩猎采集者生活的信息，远比其平凡的外表所暗示的要丰富得多。

sents.en: When an abstract-looking ivory artifact emerged from the Hohle Fels cave in southern Germany in 2015, archaeologists didn’t know quite what to make of it.
sents.zh: 2015年，当一件外形抽象的象牙制品从德国南部的霍勒费尔斯洞穴出土时，考古学家并不太清楚该如何解读它。

sents.en: At first glance, the strange new discovery—a nearly eight-inch rod perforated with four small holes—seemed comparatively unspectacular.
sents.zh: 乍一看，这一奇特的新发现——一根近八英寸长、穿有四个小孔的杆状物——似乎相对而言并不起眼。

sents.en: But it has since revealed far more about the lives of Europe’s prehistoric hunter-gatherers than its unassuming appearance might have suggested.
sents.zh: 但此后它所揭示的关于欧洲史前狩猎采集者生活的信息，远比其平凡的外表所暗示的要丰富得多。

paragraphs.en: Fashioned from the tusk of a mammoth more than 35,000 years ago, this baton—a type of artifact called a lochstab —was initially interpreted as a symbolic object associated with prestige or power. But Nicholas Conard , whose team discovered the item, wasn’t so sure.
paragraphs.zh: 这根指挥棒由一根 35,000 多年前猛犸象的长牙制成——这是一类被称为「Lochstab（棍棒）」的器物——最初被解读为与威望或权力相关的象征性物品。 但发现该物品的团队负责人尼古拉斯·康纳德（Nicholas Conard）却不这么确定。

sents.en: Fashioned from the tusk of a mammoth more than 35,000 years ago, this baton—a type of artifact called a lochstab —was initially interpreted as a symbolic object associated with prestige or power.
sents.zh: 这根指挥棒由一根 35,000 多年前猛犸象的长牙制成——这是一类被称为「Lochstab（棍棒）」的器物——最初被解读为与威望或权力相关的象征性物品。

sents.en: But Nicholas Conard , whose team discovered the item, wasn’t so sure.
sents.zh: 但发现该物品的团队负责人尼古拉斯·康纳德（Nicholas Conard）却不这么确定。

paragraphs.en: Noticing that each of the baton’s holes was lined with carefully carved spiral grooves, he began to suspect that the lochstab might have been a tool used by twisting some other material through the perforations. “If you’re pushing something through a hole and rotating it ... you’re very quickly in the world of fiber,” says Conard, an archaeologist at the University of Tübingen in Germany. Sure enough, when he and his colleagues tried threading cattail fibers through these holes, they found that the grooves helped to orient the strands . Within ten minutes, the group had woven the fibers into 16 feet of thick, strong rope.
paragraphs.zh: 他注意到指挥棒上的每个孔内都刻有精心雕凿的螺旋凹槽，于是开始怀疑这根“洛赫施塔布”可能是一种工具，使用时将其他材料穿过孔洞并旋转。“如果你把某样东西穿过孔并转动它……你很快就会进入纤维的世界，”德国图宾根大学的考古学家科纳德说。 果不其然，当他和同事们尝试将香蒲纤维穿过这些孔洞时，他们发现这些凹槽有助于将纤维束定向。 不到十分钟，这个团队就将这些纤维编成了16英尺长、粗壮结实的绳子。

sents.en: Sure enough, when he and his colleagues tried threading cattail fibers through these holes, they found that the grooves helped to orient the strands .
sents.zh: 果不其然，当他和同事们尝试将香蒲纤维穿过这些孔洞时，他们发现这些凹槽有助于将纤维束定向。

sents.zh: 不到十分钟，这个团队就将这些纤维编成了16英尺长、粗壮结实的绳子。

paragraphs.en: Yet while these experiments might have helped to solve one archaeological mystery, they also highlighted a much larger problem. The inhabitants of Hohle Fels must have manufactured significant quantities of rope, but none of it has survived. All that remains is the most durable component of this ancient production system—the ivory lochstab.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，尽管这些实验可能有助于解开一个考古之谜，它们也突显了一个大得多的问题。 霍勒费尔斯的居民必定制造过大量的绳索，但没有任何一件保存下来。 留存至今的只有这一古老生产体系中最耐用的部件——象牙制的lochstab。

sents.en: Yet while these experiments might have helped to solve one archaeological mystery, they also highlighted a much larger problem.
sents.zh: 然而，尽管这些实验可能有助于解开一个考古之谜，它们也突显了一个大得多的问题。

sents.en: The inhabitants of Hohle Fels must have manufactured significant quantities of rope, but none of it has survived.
sents.zh: 霍勒费尔斯的居民必定制造过大量的绳索，但没有任何一件保存下来。

sents.en: All that remains is the most durable component of this ancient production system—the ivory lochstab.
sents.zh: 留存至今的只有这一古老生产体系中最耐用的部件——象牙制的lochstab。

paragraphs.en: “There’s certainly a lot of bias in what we’re viewing in the archaeological record, because we are focusing on the things that preserve,” says paleoanthropologist Emma Finestone at the Cleveland Museum of Natural History. As a consequence, archaeologists rely heavily on stone tools and bone artifacts to reconstruct our prehistory, while objects made from less durable plant and animal products remain largely overlooked. Yet these soft technologies played a huge role in shaping the survival strategies and daily lives of our ancestors.
paragraphs.zh: 克利夫兰自然历史博物馆的古人类学家艾玛·芬尼斯通说：“我们在考古记录中所看到的内容肯定存在很大的偏差，因为我们关注的是那些能够保存下来的东西。” 因此，考古学家在很大程度上依赖石器与骨器来重建人类的史前历史，而由耐久性较差的植物和动物制品制成的器物则大多被忽视。 然而，这些柔软的技术在塑造我们祖先的生存策略和日常生活中发挥了巨大作用。

sents.en: “There’s certainly a lot of bias in what we’re viewing in the archaeological record, because we are focusing on the things that preserve,” says paleoanthropologist Emma Finestone at the Cleveland Museum of Natural History.
sents.zh: 克利夫兰自然历史博物馆的古人类学家艾玛·芬尼斯通说：“我们在考古记录中所看到的内容肯定存在很大的偏差，因为我们关注的是那些能够保存下来的东西。”

sents.en: As a consequence, archaeologists rely heavily on stone tools and bone artifacts to reconstruct our prehistory, while objects made from less durable plant and animal products remain largely overlooked.
sents.zh: 因此，考古学家在很大程度上依赖石器与骨器来重建人类的史前历史，而由耐久性较差的植物和动物制品制成的器物则大多被忽视。

sents.en: Yet these soft technologies played a huge role in shaping the survival strategies and daily lives of our ancestors.
sents.zh: 然而，这些柔软的技术在塑造我们祖先的生存策略和日常生活中发挥了巨大作用。

paragraphs.en: “We’re missing 90 percent-plus of what is happening during a [prehistoric] day, and a lot of that uses technology that we don’t think about,” says Bruce Hardy , a paleoanthropologist at Kenyon College in Ohio. The problem facing archaeologists, therefore, is how to study a technology that is, in a sense, invisible—a technology they can’t actually find.
paragraphs.zh: 「我们遗漏了（史前）一天中所发生的事情的90%以上，其中很多东西涉及我们从未想过的技术，」俄亥俄州凯尼恩学院的古人类学家布鲁斯·哈迪说。 因此，考古学家面临的问题是如何研究一种在某种意义上不可见的技术——一种他们实际上无法找到的技术。

sents.en: “We’re missing 90 percent-plus of what is happening during a [prehistoric] day, and a lot of that uses technology that we don’t think about,” says Bruce Hardy , a paleoanthropologist at Kenyon College in Ohio.
sents.zh: 「我们遗漏了（史前）一天中所发生的事情的90%以上，其中很多东西涉及我们从未想过的技术，」俄亥俄州凯尼恩学院的古人类学家布鲁斯·哈迪说。

sents.en: The problem facing archaeologists, therefore, is how to study a technology that is, in a sense, invisible—a technology they can’t actually find.
sents.zh: 因此，考古学家面临的问题是如何研究一种在某种意义上不可见的技术——一种他们实际上无法找到的技术。

paragraphs.en: The oldest surviving example of human-made fiber is a six-millimeter-long piece of string made by Neanderthals some 50,000 years ago. It’s an exceedingly rare example of preserved ancient fiber , and how it managed to withstand the ravages of time isn’t clear. Discovered by Hardy and his colleagues at the Abri du Maras rock shelter in France, this small length of three-ply cord indicates that fiber has deep roots in the human lineage.
paragraphs.zh: 目前保存至今最古老的人造纤维标本，是一段由尼安德特人在约五万年前制作的、长六毫米的绳线。 这是保存下来的古代纤维中极为罕见的标本，而它如何经受住时间的侵蚀尚不清楚。 这段三股搓成的小绳由哈迪及其同事在法国的阿布里杜马拉斯岩棚遗址发现，它表明纤维技艺在人类谱系中有着深远的根源。

sents.en: The oldest surviving example of human-made fiber is a six-millimeter-long piece of string made by Neanderthals some 50,000 years ago.
sents.zh: 目前保存至今最古老的人造纤维标本，是一段由尼安德特人在约五万年前制作的、长六毫米的绳线。

sents.en: It’s an exceedingly rare example of preserved ancient fiber , and how it managed to withstand the ravages of time isn’t clear.
sents.zh: 这是保存下来的古代纤维中极为罕见的标本，而它如何经受住时间的侵蚀尚不清楚。

sents.en: Discovered by Hardy and his colleagues at the Abri du Maras rock shelter in France, this small length of three-ply cord indicates that fiber has deep roots in the human lineage.
sents.zh: 这段三股搓成的小绳由哈迪及其同事在法国的阿布里杜马拉斯岩棚遗址发现，它表明纤维技艺在人类谱系中有着深远的根源。

paragraphs.en: “This is probably a very old technology that goes way back much further than this, back to an ancestor shared by modern humans and Neanderthals,” Hardy says. In other words, more than half a million years ago .
paragraphs.zh: “这可能是一项非常古老的技术，其起源远比这个年代更早，可以追溯到现代人类与尼安德特人的共同祖先，”哈迪说。 换句话说，那是在五十多万年前。

sents.en: “This is probably a very old technology that goes way back much further than this, back to an ancestor shared by modern humans and Neanderthals,” Hardy says.
sents.zh: “这可能是一项非常古老的技术，其起源远比这个年代更早，可以追溯到现代人类与尼安德特人的共同祖先，”哈迪说。

sents.en: In other words, more than half a million years ago .
sents.zh: 换句话说，那是在五十多万年前。

paragraphs.en: So far, the oldest evidence of fiber use dates back about 250,000 years, inferred from markings on stone tools from France and the Netherlands. The marks suggest the tools may have been hafted, or attached to a handle with some type of string or cord. While the bindings have long since decomposed, the traces they left behind hint that fiber technologies aided the survival of the prehistoric human species that occupied Europe long before Homo sapiens got a foothold on the continent 45,000 years ago.
paragraphs.zh: 迄今为止，关于纤维使用的最古老证据可追溯至约25万年前，这一结论是从法国和荷兰的石器上的痕迹推断出来的。 这些痕迹表明，这些石器可能曾被装柄，即用某种类型的绳线或绳索固定到手柄上。 虽然这些绑扎物早已分解，但它们留下的痕迹暗示，纤维技术帮助了曾占据欧洲的史前人类物种的生存——远在智人于4.5万年前在这片大陆上站稳脚跟之前。

sents.en: So far, the oldest evidence of fiber use dates back about 250,000 years, inferred from markings on stone tools from France and the Netherlands.
sents.zh: 迄今为止，关于纤维使用的最古老证据可追溯至约25万年前，这一结论是从法国和荷兰的石器上的痕迹推断出来的。

sents.en: The marks suggest the tools may have been hafted, or attached to a handle with some type of string or cord.
sents.zh: 这些痕迹表明，这些石器可能曾被装柄，即用某种类型的绳线或绳索固定到手柄上。

sents.en: While the bindings have long since decomposed, the traces they left behind hint that fiber technologies aided the survival of the prehistoric human species that occupied Europe long before Homo sapiens got a foothold on the continent 45,000 years ago.
sents.zh: 虽然这些绑扎物早已分解，但它们留下的痕迹暗示，纤维技术帮助了曾占据欧洲的史前人类物种的生存——远在智人于4.5万年前在这片大陆上站稳脚跟之前。

paragraphs.en: The invention of hafting may represent a “revolutionary moment” in our technological history, says Veerle Rots , an archaeologist at the University of Liège in Belgium who led the experimental work on the Hohle Fels lochstab. “It fundamentally changes the use of stone tools and allows a whole range of new possibilities in how you’re conceptualizing a tool,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: 比利时列日大学的考古学家薇尔勒·罗茨主持了关于霍勒费尔斯棍棒的实验研究。她说，柄装技术的发明可能代表了我们技术史上的一个「革命性时刻」。「它从根本上改变了石器工具的使用方式，并让你在构想一件工具时拥有全新的可能性。」她说。

paragraphs.en: A sharpened stone point, for example, suddenly becomes part of a hunting weapon when hafted onto a wooden shaft. A stone handax can be wielded with significantly greater force and from a wider range of angles once fastened onto a handle. What made cordage like rope, string and twine so transformative, therefore, was that it connected other technologies together to radically expand what prehistoric humans could build, carry and hunt.
paragraphs.zh: 例如，一个磨尖的石制尖头，一旦被安装在木柄上，就会突然成为狩猎武器的一部分。 石制手斧一旦被固定到手柄上，就能以明显更大的力量、从更广的角度范围被挥舞使用。 因此，像绳索、细绳和麻线这样的绳具之所以具有如此变革性，在于它将其他技术连接在一起，极大地扩展了史前人类能够建造、携带和狩猎的能力。

sents.en: A sharpened stone point, for example, suddenly becomes part of a hunting weapon when hafted onto a wooden shaft.
sents.zh: 例如，一个磨尖的石制尖头，一旦被安装在木柄上，就会突然成为狩猎武器的一部分。

sents.en: A stone handax can be wielded with significantly greater force and from a wider range of angles once fastened onto a handle.
sents.zh: 石制手斧一旦被固定到手柄上，就能以明显更大的力量、从更广的角度范围被挥舞使用。

sents.en: What made cordage like rope, string and twine so transformative, therefore, was that it connected other technologies together to radically expand what prehistoric humans could build, carry and hunt.
sents.zh: 因此，像绳索、细绳和麻线这样的绳具之所以具有如此变革性，在于它将其他技术连接在一起，极大地扩展了史前人类能够建造、携带和狩猎的能力。

paragraphs.en: The transport of stone for making tools, for instance, was an essential logistical operation that may have depended on soft materials from the very beginning. According to Finestone’s research, toolmaking hominins moved high-quality stones over long distances as early as three million years ago —cumbersome loads that would have been very difficult to transport with bare hands alone.
paragraphs.zh: 例如，用于制造工具的石材运输，就是一项至关重要的后勤作业，它可能从一开始就依赖于柔软材料。 根据芬斯通（Finestone）的研究，早在三百万年前，制造工具的人科动物就已经开始长途搬运优质石材——这些笨重的负载仅凭赤手搬运将非常困难。

sents.en: The transport of stone for making tools, for instance, was an essential logistical operation that may have depended on soft materials from the very beginning.
sents.zh: 例如，用于制造工具的石材运输，就是一项至关重要的后勤作业，它可能从一开始就依赖于柔软材料。

sents.en: According to Finestone’s research, toolmaking hominins moved high-quality stones over long distances as early as three million years ago —cumbersome loads that would have been very difficult to transport with bare hands alone.
sents.zh: 根据芬斯通（Finestone）的研究，早在三百万年前，制造工具的人科动物就已经开始长途搬运优质石材——这些笨重的负载仅凭赤手搬运将非常困难。

paragraphs.en: “It would have been really helpful to them to have some mechanism for carrying cobbles,” she says. Such receptacles have never been found. But if they were used, they were probably made from perishable materials like leather and fiber.
paragraphs.zh: “要是当时有某种搬运鹅卵石的装置，那对他们来说会非常有帮助，”她说。 这样的容器从未被发现过。 但如果它们确实被使用过，它们很可能是由皮革和纤维等易腐烂材料制成的。

sents.en: “It would have been really helpful to them to have some mechanism for carrying cobbles,” she says.
sents.zh: “要是当时有某种搬运鹅卵石的装置，那对他们来说会非常有帮助，”她说。

sents.en: Such receptacles have never been found.
sents.zh: 这样的容器从未被发现过。

sents.en: But if they were used, they were probably made from perishable materials like leather and fiber.
sents.zh: 但如果它们确实被使用过，它们很可能是由皮革和纤维等易腐烂材料制成的。

paragraphs.en: Cordage likely also aided our ancestors by enabling passive hunting with snares and nets. Unlike handheld weapons, these tools could catch prey in the user’s absence, allowing hunter-gatherers to focus on other tasks. Rock art in Spain from around 7,500 years ago even appears to depict people climbing sophisticated rope ladders to access beehives, illustrating how fiber technologies opened up new foraging opportunities.
paragraphs.zh: 绳索很可能也帮助了我们的祖先，使他们能够借助陷阱和网进行被动式狩猎。 与手持武器不同，这些工具可以在使用者不在场的情况下捕获猎物，让狩猎采集者能够专注于其他任务。 西班牙大约 7,500 年前的岩石艺术甚至似乎描绘了人们攀爬精巧的绳梯去获取蜂巢的情景，这说明纤维技术开辟了新的觅食机会。

sents.en: Cordage likely also aided our ancestors by enabling passive hunting with snares and nets.
sents.zh: 绳索很可能也帮助了我们的祖先，使他们能够借助陷阱和网进行被动式狩猎。

sents.en: Unlike handheld weapons, these tools could catch prey in the user’s absence, allowing hunter-gatherers to focus on other tasks.
sents.zh: 与手持武器不同，这些工具可以在使用者不在场的情况下捕获猎物，让狩猎采集者能够专注于其他任务。

sents.en: Rock art in Spain from around 7,500 years ago even appears to depict people climbing sophisticated rope ladders to access beehives, illustrating how fiber technologies opened up new foraging opportunities.
sents.zh: 西班牙大约 7,500 年前的岩石艺术甚至似乎描绘了人们攀爬精巧的绳梯去获取蜂巢的情景，这说明纤维技术开辟了新的觅食机会。

paragraphs.en: “Once you figure out this technology, you’re just going to keep applying it,” says Hardy. “You’re going to become dependent on it.”
paragraphs.zh: 哈迪说：“一旦你弄懂了这项技术，你就会不断地使用它。你会变得依赖它。”

paragraphs.en: Did you know? The earliest physical evidence of sewing
paragraphs.zh: 你知道吗？ 关于缝纫最早的实物证据

sents.en: Did you know?
sents.zh: 你知道吗？

sents.en: The earliest physical evidence of sewing
sents.zh: 关于缝纫最早的实物证据

paragraphs.en: In a cave in Oregon, researchers discovered two pieces of 12,000-year-old elk hide stitched together with a cord —the oldest known remains of sewn animal hide . (Indirect evidence of sewing, such as needles with eyes for threading string, has been found from longer ago throughout the world.)
paragraphs.zh: 在俄勒冈州的一个洞穴里，研究人员发现了两片用绳线缝在一起的12,000年前的麋鹿皮——这是已知最古老的缝制兽皮遗存。 （更早的缝纫间接证据，例如带有穿线孔的针，已在世界各地被发现。）

sents.en: In a cave in Oregon, researchers discovered two pieces of 12,000-year-old elk hide stitched together with a cord —the oldest known remains of sewn animal hide .
sents.zh: 在俄勒冈州的一个洞穴里，研究人员发现了两片用绳线缝在一起的12,000年前的麋鹿皮——这是已知最古老的缝制兽皮遗存。

sents.en: (Indirect evidence of sewing, such as needles with eyes for threading string, has been found from longer ago throughout the world.)
sents.zh: （更早的缝纫间接证据，例如带有穿线孔的针，已在世界各地被发现。）

paragraphs.en: As cordage became essential for survival, the need to continually produce it fundamentally shaped the daily routines of ancient hunter-gatherers, Hardy says.
paragraphs.zh: Hardy 说，随着绳索成为生存的必需品，持续生产绳索的需求从根本上塑造了古代狩猎采集者的日常生活。

paragraphs.en: “You find out very rapidly that you need a lot of footage of cord in order to make anything,” he says. One year in a class he taught, Hardy and his students built a raft out of sycamore saplings lashed together with what he estimates was just over 100 yards of rope. “It was hours and hours and hours of making cordage to do that.”
paragraphs.zh: “你会很快发现，要做任何东西都需要大量的绳索素材，”他说。 在他教过的一门课中，有一年哈迪和学生们用小树苗捆扎成一只木筏，据他估计用了刚超过100码的绳索。“那需要花上好几个小时又好几个小时来制作绳索。”

sents.en: “You find out very rapidly that you need a lot of footage of cord in order to make anything,” he says.
sents.zh: “你会很快发现，要做任何东西都需要大量的绳索素材，”他说。

sents.en: One year in a class he taught, Hardy and his students built a raft out of sycamore saplings lashed together with what he estimates was just over 100 yards of rope. “It was hours and hours and hours of making cordage to do that.”
sents.zh: 在他教过的一门课中，有一年哈迪和学生们用小树苗捆扎成一只木筏，据他估计用了刚超过100码的绳索。“那需要花上好几个小时又好几个小时来制作绳索。”

paragraphs.en: Ethnographic studies of present-day traditional societies attest to the labor involved. The Wola of Papua New Guinea, for example, incorporate string or fibers into 95 percent of the items they produce, from hunting weapons to musical instruments. Anthropologists have found that it takes the Wola between 65 and 80 hours of twisting to generate enough string to manufacture a single bag—and that’s on top of 14 hours of foraging to collect the raw materials. Given that the Wola live in permanent villages, this time investment may not present any major issues, but for nomadic hunter-gatherers, the need to produce such enormous quantities of cordage would have significantly impacted their ability to move around.
paragraphs.zh: 对当今传统社会的人类学研究证实了其中所涉及的劳动量。 例如，巴布亚新几内亚的沃拉人所生产的物品中有95%都含有绳线或纤维，从狩猎武器到乐器皆是如此。 人类学家发现，沃拉人需要花费65到80个小时捻线，才能制造出足够制作一个袋子的绳线——而这还不算为采集原材料所需的14个小时的觅食时间。 鉴于沃拉人定居在固定的村落中，这种时间投入也许不会构成什么大问题，但对于游牧的狩猎采集者而言，生产如此大量绳索的需求将严重影响他们的迁徙能力。

sents.zh: 对当今传统社会的人类学研究证实了其中所涉及的劳动量。

sents.zh: 人类学家发现，沃拉人需要花费65到80个小时捻线，才能制造出足够制作一个袋子的绳线——而这还不算为采集原材料所需的14个小时的觅食时间。

sents.en: Given that the Wola live in permanent villages, this time investment may not present any major issues, but for nomadic hunter-gatherers, the need to produce such enormous quantities of cordage would have significantly impacted their ability to move around.

paragraphs.en: The Neanderthals of Abri du Maras, for example, made their cord from the inner bark of pine or another conifer, which can be harvested only in the spring and early summer, when the sap begins to rise and the inner bark thickens. Once collected, the bark must be soaked in water for about two weeks before it can be broken up into usable fibers.
paragraphs.zh: 例如，阿布里·杜·马拉斯遗址的尼安德特人用松树或其他针叶树的内层树皮制作绳索，而这种树皮只能在春季和初夏采集，因为此时树液开始上升，内层树皮才会变厚。 树皮采集后，必须先在水中浸泡大约两周，才能被分解成可用的纤维。

sents.en: The Neanderthals of Abri du Maras, for example, made their cord from the inner bark of pine or another conifer, which can be harvested only in the spring and early summer, when the sap begins to rise and the inner bark thickens.
sents.zh: 例如，阿布里·杜·马拉斯遗址的尼安德特人用松树或其他针叶树的内层树皮制作绳索，而这种树皮只能在春季和初夏采集，因为此时树液开始上升，内层树皮才会变厚。

sents.en: Once collected, the bark must be soaked in water for about two weeks before it can be broken up into usable fibers.
sents.zh: 树皮采集后，必须先在水中浸泡大约两周，才能被分解成可用的纤维。

paragraphs.en: The lengthy nature of this process would therefore have dictated the seasonal work schedule of mobile hunter-gatherers, who would not be able to move on until a sufficient quantity of cordage had been manufactured. “It’s going to be impacting your daily life,” says Hardy. “You’re going to be making cordage all the time, at least during certain times of year, and storing it up.”
paragraphs.zh: 这一过程的漫长性质决定了流动的狩猎采集者的季节性工作安排，他们在制造出足够数量的绳索之前无法继续迁移。哈迪说：“这会影响你的日常生活。你会一直在制作绳索，至少在一年中的某些时候如此，并将其储存起来。”

paragraphs.en: So, while stone flakes for use as cutting tools, scrapers and weapons could be struck from larger chunks of flint whenever needed, activities like rope making, hide tanning and woodworking required seasonal planning, sustained labor and group decision-making.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，虽然用作切割工具、刮削器和武器的石片可以随时从较大的燧石块上敲击下来，但像制绳、鞣制兽皮和木工这样的活动则需要季节性的规划、持续的劳动以及群体决策。

paragraphs.en: The more researchers discover about these soft materials, the more they understand about how these technologies defined the rhythm of everyday life in the Stone Age , the large swath of human history from about 3.3 million to 4,000 years ago. “We’ll learn some new stuff from stone tools and from animal bones, but we’re not going to see this other side of daily life that is going on unless we can see the perishable material,” says Hardy.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员对这些软质材料了解得越多，就越能理解这些技术如何定义了石器时代日常生活的节奏——石器时代是人类历史的广阔时期，大约从330万年前延续到4000年前。哈迪（Hardy）说：“我们会从石器和动物骨骼中学到一些新东西，但除非能看到那些易腐烂的材料，否则我们无法看到日常生活中正在发生的另一面。”

paragraphs.en: That material isn’t just limited to fiber. At an ancient lakeshore exposed by a mine near Schöningen, Germany, archaeologists discovered a remarkable assemblage of 300,000-year-old wooden spears , along with bones of some of the horses and other animals they were used to kill. The spears survived because anaerobic conditions at the waterlogged site prevented microorganisms from breaking them down. Made by an extinct human species, these remarkable weapons were expertly worked into aerodynamic forms, thus enhancing their lethality and revealing a level of technological sophistication that stone tools alone fail to capture.
paragraphs.zh: 这些材料并不仅限于纤维。 在德国舍宁根附近一处矿井暴露出的古湖岸，考古学家发现了一批非凡的30万年前的木质长矛，同时出土的还有这些长矛所猎杀的部分马匹及其他动物的骨骼。 这些长矛得以保存下来，是因为该遗址长期浸水的环境形成了缺氧条件，阻止了微生物将其分解。 这些非凡的武器由一个已灭绝的人种制造，经过精湛加工而呈流线型，从而提升了杀伤力，并展现出仅凭石器无法体现的技术造诣。

sents.en: That material isn’t just limited to fiber.
sents.zh: 这些材料并不仅限于纤维。

sents.en: The spears survived because anaerobic conditions at the waterlogged site prevented microorganisms from breaking them down.
sents.zh: 这些长矛得以保存下来，是因为该遗址长期浸水的环境形成了缺氧条件，阻止了微生物将其分解。

sents.en: Made by an extinct human species, these remarkable weapons were expertly worked into aerodynamic forms, thus enhancing their lethality and revealing a level of technological sophistication that stone tools alone fail to capture.
sents.zh: 这些非凡的武器由一个已灭绝的人种制造，经过精湛加工而呈流线型，从而提升了杀伤力，并展现出仅凭石器无法体现的技术造诣。

paragraphs.en: At Schöningen, “you see how the stone articulates with the animal resources and the botanical resources, so you can see that the connections between stone, plant and animal resources are all essential,” says Conard, who currently directs the excavation of the site.
paragraphs.zh: 在舍宁根（Schöningen），「你可以看到石器如何与动物资源和植物资源相互关联，因此你能看到石器、植物与动物资源之间的联系都至关重要，」目前主持该遗址发掘工作的科纳德（Conard）说道。

paragraphs.en: Sites like Hohle Fels, Abri du Maras and Schöningen provide glimpses into a far richer technological world, reminding us of what’s missing from the archaeological record, says Conard. “It’s only called the Stone Age because all we find is stone, not because there was only stone.”
paragraphs.zh: 康纳德（Conard）说，像霍勒费尔斯（Hohle Fels）、马拉斯岩棚（Abri du Maras）和舍宁根（Schöningen）这样的遗址让我们得以窥见一个远比想象中更丰富的技术世界，提醒我们考古记录中缺失了什么。“之所以称之为石器时代，只是因为我们能找到的只有石头，而不是因为当时只有石头。”
